subject.title: fix(deepgram): validate realtime base URL overrides, preserving ws(s):// endpoints

question: Should an explicit Deepgram `ws://` base URL become a supported plaintext transport, or should the released secure upgrade remain in force?
rationale: Plaintext support is not required to fix malformed URLs or preserve released `wss://` endpoints, and permitting it changes the security boundary for provider audio and authentication traffic.

options.title: Keep Secure Upgrade
options.body: Preserve direct `wss://`, but continue mapping `ws://` to `wss://` and update the new tests and proof accordingly.

options.title: Support Plaintext WebSocket
options.body: Preserve `ws://` only with explicit owner approval, operator-facing documentation, and focused security and upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Keep Secure Upgrade
recommendation.body: Preserve direct `wss://`, but continue mapping `ws://` to `wss://` and update the new tests and proof accordingly.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties Vincent Koc most directly to Deepgram and shared realtime-transcription behavior.
